lines.text: Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. Amy gets a dimmer.
lines.script: [brisk, cheerful] Rewiring the hallway. Amy wanted a dimmer. [level, knowing] Amy gets a dimmer.

lines.text: Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [direct, distracted] Tom. Hey. Hold this. No, the other end. [quick, warning] Don't touch the copper.

lines.text: Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? Both. Correct. Go get 'em.
lines.script: [goofy, proud] Grace, Rose, come here. Who's Daddy's favorite? [brisk, pleased] Both. Correct. Go get 'em.

lines.text: Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. Also, why are you sticky?
lines.script: [beaming, direct] Grace, you were amazing out there. Rose, you were also amazing. [puzzled, wary] Also, why are you sticky?

lines.text: Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. Before lunch.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, bragging] Fixed the porch light, the garbage disposal and the bunk bed. [smug, level] Before lunch.

lines.text: Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. I got a truck and two girls. Living the song.
lines.script: [level, amused] Every country song is about a truck, a dog or a girl. [direct, pleased] I got a truck and two girls. [dry, sincere] Living the song.

lines.text: Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. It was a playoff game. We lost.
lines.script: [dry, deadpan] Amy says I never sit down. I sat down once. [proud, level] It was a playoff game. [grim, flat] We lost.

lines.text: Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. And I built that deck.
lines.script: [soft, sincere] Those two girls are the best thing I ever built. [proud, amused] And I built that deck.

lines.text: Long Island born. Country music raised. Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.
lines.script: [level, matter-of-fact] Long Island born. Country music raised. [amused, dry] Don't ask me how. Nobody knows.

lines.text: Big game tonight. If you hear yelling, that's me. If you hear crying, that's also me.
lines.script: [hyped, bright] Big game tonight. [gleeful, level] If you hear yelling, that's me. [mock-serious, deadpan] If you hear crying, that's also me.

lines.text: Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. I know. It's on the list.
lines.script: [calm, level] Watch your step, Tom. That board is loose. [sheepish, rueful] I know. It's on the list.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. That's allowed. It's in the contract.
lines.script: [low, conspiratorial] Halverson. Fourth grade. I'm hiding in the staff room. [deadpan, flat] That's allowed. ...It's in the contract.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: If you're hungry, the fridge is a minefield. Every lunch in there has a name on it. Read the labels.
lines.script: [deadpan, warning] If you're hungry, the fridge is a MINEFIELD. [flat, grave] Every lunch in there has a name on it. ...Read the labels.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Conference night is over. I survived. I'm going to sit on this couch until Field Day.
lines.script: [exhausted, relieved] Conference night is over. I SURVIVED. [deadpan, weary] I'm going to sit on this couch... until Field Day.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Deedee’s plate? Oh, everybody waits for Deedee’s plate. She brings one every conference night.
lines.script: [brightening, reverent] Deedee’s plate? Oh, EVERYBODY waits for Deedee’s plate. [direct, sincere] She brings one every conference night.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Don't tell Gary. Gary eats the whole thing.
lines.script: [hushed, conspiratorial] Don't tell Gary. [deadpan, annoyed] Gary eats the WHOLE thing.

lines.text: Heading out? I can come. I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion about whatever you're about to fight.
lines.script: [level, eager] Heading out? I can come. [direct, goofy] I have a tool belt, a flashlight and a strong opinion [deadpan, level] about whatever you're about to fight.

lines.text: No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. It's been almost done since June.
lines.script: [level, dry] No problem. The hallway light won't finish itself. [rueful, flat] It's been almost done since June.

lines.text: Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. I'll be on the ladder.
lines.script: [level, amused] Somebody has to tag out. I'll wait. [level, direct] I'll be on the ladder.

lines.text: Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. Don't ask about the ladder.
lines.script: [direct, cheerful] Great. Let me grab my jacket. And the ladder. [firm, dry] Don't ask about the ladder.

lines.text: Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. So I came back too. I brought bread.
lines.script: [cheerful, relieved] Hey, everybody. The lights all came back on at twelve oh one. [direct, level] So I came back too. [sheepish, quiet] I brought bread.

lines.text: It's store-bought.
lines.script: [flat, guilty] It's store-bought.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Take some for the road. Don't tell Gary.
lines.script: [direct, sincere] Take some for the road. [hushed, conspiratorial] ...Don't tell Gary.

lines.speaker: Mr. Halverson
lines.text: Every conference night. Twelve years. It's the only reason Gary shows up.
lines.script: [tired, sincere] Every conference night. TWELVE years. [deadpan, flat] ...It's the only reason Gary shows up.

lines.text: The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [satisfied, level] The banner's done. Hold this. No, the other end. [sharp, warning] Don't touch the copper.

lines.text: It lights up. Every letter. I'm an electrician, Gracie. It was never going to just hang there.
lines.script: [proud, bright] It lights up. Every letter. [sincere, mock-offended] I'm an electrician, Gracie. [level, certain] It was never going to just hang there.

lines.text: Hold this. No, the other end. It's the OTHER banner. Don't touch the copper.
lines.script: [brisk, distracted] Hold this. No, the other end. [emphatic, quick] It's the OTHER banner. [sharp, warning] Don't touch the copper.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. He catches one every time. It's always THIS big.
lines.script: [earnest, hushed] He said if you were late he'd catch the fish without you. [bright, certain] He catches one every time. [proud, loud] It's always THIS big.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we'd better hurry, before it gets any bigger.
lines.script: [dry, calm] Then we'd better hurry... before it gets any bigger.

lines.speaker: Reel
lines.text: Your father has been fishing this pier since before the pier. He catches something every day. The size, I round down.
lines.script: [slow, fond] Your father has been fishing this pier since BEFORE the pier. He catches something every day. [deadpan, knowing] The size, I round down.

lines.text: Here, take my spare cap. For luck. I caught a twelve pounder in it. Nine. It was a big six.
lines.script: [tender] Here, take my spare cap. For luck. [proud, boastful] I caught a twelve pounder in it. [grudging, quieter] Nine. It was a big six.

lines.text: My favorite son!
lines.script: [delighted, warm] My favorite son!

lines.text: My favorite son! And my girls! Come here, come here.
lines.script: [overjoyed, bustling] My favorite son! And my girls! [warm, urgent] Come here, come here.

lines.text: Tom, you must be starving! Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.
lines.script: [warm, fussing] Tom, you must be starving! [brisk, firm] Sit. The crisp needs ten minutes on the counter.

lines.text: My favorite son! And my girls! And my... oh. OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.
lines.script: [delighted, warm] My favorite son! And my girls! [trailing, puzzled] And my... oh. [alarmed, bewildered] OH. Why is Rose in an ice cube.

lines.text: Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for the job of a dad. Not even AI wants that!
lines.script: [calm, wry] Olivia writes about AI taking jobs. Nobody is coming for the job of a dad. [deadpan, tired] Not even AI wants that!

lines.text: Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it.
lines.script: [easy, sheepish] Also, your starter was bubbling out of the jar, so I baked a boule with it.

lines.text: He's been saying that for a while, babe.
lines.script: [low, dry] He's been saying that for a while, babe.

lines.text: Main event. I'll take it.
lines.script: [amused, easy] Main event. I'll take it.

lines.text: Spooky. I love it. Let's go check on Mr. Washington.
lines.script: [amused, uneasy] Spooky. I love it. [cautious, steady] Let's go check on Mr. Washington.

lines.text: Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. Look at those bubbles.
lines.script: [focused, murmuring] Fifty grams of flour, fifty grams of water. Stir. [soft, delighted] Look at those bubbles.

lines.text: I flew three thousand miles to see you... and maybe the starter.
lines.script: [quickly, warm] I flew three thousand miles to see you... [teasing, low] and maybe the starter.

lines.text: I'm proud. As long as you didn't spin it on your pottery wheel.
lines.script: [dry, mock-offended] I'm proud. [deadpan, grudging] As long as you didn't spin it on your pottery wheel.

lines.text: Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. So polite!
lines.script: [listing out] Sit, paw, treat. She knows the whole routine. [warm, proud] So polite!

lines.text: TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.
lines.script: [dry, mild] TNB said he'd be home. Spring Street loft.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Airport? Hop in. Cab seven has been waiting all day.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Airport? Hop in. [fond, drawn out] Cab seven has been waiting ALL day.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The girls stay put. Amy's orders. I follow Amy's orders. Everybody does.
lines.script: [quick, matter-of-fact] The girls stay put. Amy's orders. [flat, meek] I follow Amy's orders. ...EVERYBODY does.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: LAX it is. Seat belts. Your niece is giving me the look.
lines.script: [quick, cheerful] LAX it is. Seat belts. [deadpan, nervous] Your niece is giving me... the LOOK.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Girls, out you go. No stowaways. I checked the trunk last time.
lines.script: [quick, firm] Girls, out you go. No stowaways. [offhand, knowing] I checked the trunk last time.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Off to the airport. I'll take the scenic route. By scenic I mean the only route.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Off to the airport. I'll take the scenic route. [matter-of-fact, dry] By scenic I mean... the ONLY route.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The girls stay home. It's a school night. Even I know that, and I don't have kids.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] The girls stay home. It's a school night. [flat, proud] Even I know that, and I don't HAVE kids.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Airport. Los Angeles. Your usual.
lines.script: [quick, deadpan] Airport. Los Angeles. ...Your usual.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Girls, say your goodbyes. I'll keep the meter off. Mostly.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Girls, say your goodbyes. I'll keep the meter off. [offhand, mischievous] ...Mostly.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Los Angeles? Sure. I'll get you there before the sun gets bored.
lines.script: [quick, cheerful] Los Angeles? Sure. [matter-of-fact, breezy] I'll get you there before the sun gets BORED.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The girls stay here. Amy's rule number one. There are about forty more.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] The girls stay here. Amy's rule number one. [flat, weary] ...There are about FORTY more.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Another flight, another gold star for cab seven.
lines.script: [proud, deadpan] Another flight, another gold star... for cab seven.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: The girls head home. Straight home. Do not follow the cab.
lines.script: [quick, firm] The girls head home. Straight home. [flat, stern] Do NOT follow the cab.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Airport. You've got the look of a man who packed light.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Airport. [matter-of-fact, knowing] You've got the look of a man who packed light.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Girls, back to the house. Your grandmother has pie. That's not a rumor.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Girls, back to the house. Your grandmother has PIE. [flat, grave] ...That's not a rumor.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Los Angeles again. Cab seven is ready.
lines.script: [quick, proud] Los Angeles again. Cab seven is READY.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: LAX. Sit back. The radio is on something calm.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] LAX. Sit back. [deadpan, soothing] The radio is on something... calm.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Off we go. Don't touch the visor. Everybody touches the visor.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Off we go. Don't touch the visor. [offhand, weary] ...EVERYBODY touches the visor.

lines.speaker: Sal
lines.text: Airport run. I'll have you there before your coffee gets cold.
lines.script: [quick, smug] Airport run. I'll have you there before your coffee gets cold.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Long Island? Sure. I know a shortcut. It's not shorter, but it's mine.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Long Island? Sure. I know a shortcut. [flat, proud] It's not shorter, but it's MINE.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Seat belt, please. It's decorative, but I like when people try.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Seat belt, please. [matter-of-fact, encouraging] It's decorative, but I like when people TRY.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Airport run. Cab traffic, cab snacks, cab opinions. All included.
lines.script: [quick, proud] Airport run. Cab traffic, cab snacks, cab OPINIONS. [deadpan, generous] ...All included.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: East we go. Don't mind the ketchup stain. It's from last Tuesday.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] East we go. Don't mind the ketchup stain. [offhand, matter-of-fact] ...It's from last Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: Heading home? Say hi to the Atlantic for me. The right ocean.
lines.script: [quick, friendly] Heading home? Say hi to the Atlantic for me. [flat, smug] ...The RIGHT ocean.

lines.text: Deedee! A mud blob just climbed in the window, and it's running off with your crisp!
lines.script: [alarmed, breathless] Deedee! [shrill, urgent] A mud blob just climbed in the window, and it's running off with your crisp!

lines.text: It took the crisp AND my good tin! Grab your shoes, everybody. We're going after it, and I'm coming with you.
lines.script: [outraged, fierce] It took the crisp AND my good tin! [commanding, brisk] Grab your shoes, everybody. We're going after it, and I'm coming with you.

lines.text: It's headed for Grump Hollow. I've been saying for twenty years that something lives in that pond, and nobody listens to Boppy.
lines.script: [aggrieved, vindicated] It's headed for Grump Hollow. [sulky] I've been saying for twenty years that something lives in that pond, and nobody listens to Boppy.

lines.text: I'd come with you, but my stomach is acting up. If you see the Big One in that pond, bring him back for me.
lines.script: [pained] I'd come with you, but my stomach is acting up. [brighter] If you see the Big One in that pond, bring him back for me.

lines.text: Look, rhubarb crumbs on the path. The little thief dropped them as it ran, so we can follow the trail.
lines.script: [brisk, keen] Look, rhubarb crumbs on the path. [indignant, fussing] The little thief dropped them as it ran, so we can follow the trail.

lines.text: Good job, girls. The crumb trail keeps going north, so that's the way we go.
lines.script: [proud, brisk] Good job, girls. [focused, cheerful] The crumb trail keeps going north, so that's the way we go.

lines.text: The crumbs lead around the pond, toward Boppy's fishing spot.
lines.script: [brisk, cheerful] The crumbs lead around the pond, toward Boppy's fishing spot.

lines.text: Blub. I stole it for you, boss.
lines.script: [small, eager] Blub. I stole it for you, boss.

lines.text: The tin fits on my head like a crown. I'm the king of the pond now. GLUB.
lines.script: [pompous, smug] The tin fits on my head like a crown. [gleeful, bubbling] I'm the king of the pond now. GLUB.

lines.text: We did. And when it laughed, this fell out of its lip.
lines.script: [dry, casual] We did. And when it laughed, this fell out of its lip.

lines.text: Speaking of strange. A fella was down at the pond yesterday. Long coat, in this heat. He asked how long the Big One has been alone down there.
lines.script: [wry, grumbling] Speaking of strange. A fella was down at the pond yesterday. Long coat, in this heat. He asked how long the Big One has been alone down there.

lines.text: I said twenty years. He wrote it down.
lines.script: [low, suspicious] I said twenty years. [flat, uneasy] He wrote it down.

lines.text: All yours. I like that. We'll go look at the purple sky together, but first I need one quick stop at my house.
lines.script: [soft, pleased] All yours. I like that. We'll go look at the purple sky together, but first I need one quick stop at my house.

lines.text: My sourdough starter has been alone for a week.
lines.script: [calm, steady] My sourdough starter has been alone for a week.

lines.text: The smog monsters are gone, but Mr. Washington is still in a daze. Look at him.
lines.script: [low, worried] The smog monsters are gone, but Mr. [quiet, uneasy] Washington is still in a daze. Look at him.

lines.text: Mr. Washington would never say that. The smog is doing something to him. Let's go check on Miss Odette and Doña Carmen on the boulevard.
lines.script: [dry, unsettled] Mr. [brisk, resolved] Washington would never say that. [calm, steady] The smog is doing something to him. Let's go check on Miss Odette and Doña Carmen on the boulevard.

lines.text: The smog makes people want everything to stay exactly the same forever. That's not a nice afternoon. That's a hostage situation.
lines.script: [dry, grim] The smog makes people want everything to stay exactly the same forever. [flat, deadpan] That's not a nice afternoon. [cold, dry] That's a hostage situation.

lines.text: Nara is right. That's not kitchen smoke. It's the same purple smog, and it's blowing down from the hills.
lines.script: [low, alert] Nara is right. [tense, wry] That's not kitchen smoke. It's the same purple smog, and it's blowing down from the hills.

lines.text: It's coming from the Observatory. The pipes on its side are pumping out smog like a smoke machine on a bad set.
lines.script: [dry, grim] It's coming from the Observatory. [dry, flat] The pipes on its side are pumping out smog like a smoke machine on a bad set.

lines.text: I contest that ticket, and I'm granting my own appeal. Let's keep going.
lines.script: [dry, official] I contest that ticket, and I'm granting my own appeal. [brisk, calm] Let's keep going.

lines.text: RUMBLE. A man in a long coat plugged my vents.
lines.script: [deep, sulky] RUMBLE. A man in a long coat plugged my vents.

lines.text: Now all my grumbling comes out of those pipes as purple smog, and everything it touches gets stuck. And I LIKE stuck.
lines.script: [grumbling, stubborn] Now all my grumbling comes out of those pipes as purple smog, and everything it touches gets stuck. And I LIKE stuck.

lines.text: When everything is stuck, nothing moves and nothing changes, and nobody ever has to say goodbye.
lines.script: [heavy, slow] When everything is stuck, nothing moves and nothing changes, and nobody ever has to say goodbye.

lines.text: That's what the man promised me. Nobody leaves. Not ever.
lines.script: [heavy, slow] That's what the man promised me. [aching, small] Nobody leaves. Not ever.

lines.text: So a man in a long coat plugged those vents on purpose. He wanted this whole city stuck in one afternoon. I'd like to know why.
lines.script: [dry, uneasy] So a man in a long coat plugged those vents on purpose. [low, suspicious] He wanted this whole city stuck in one afternoon. I'd like to know why.

lines.text: Long Island is home, and so is this. I have two homes. Okay. Good.
lines.script: [soft, relieved] Long Island is home, and so is this. I have two homes. [quiet, warm] Okay. Good.

lines.text: The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny's shop. He pays double, and he never takes his hat off.
lines.script: [conspiratorial, whispering] The kettle says a man in a long coat has been buying up gold coins at Penny's shop. [ominous, delighted] He pays double, and he never takes his hat off.

lines.text: Iron-Gill swam west with my jar, into the Whispering Marsh. Come on, we're going after him. And nobody walk fast.
lines.script: [determined] Iron-Gill swam west with my jar, into the Whispering Marsh. [mock-stern, bossy] Come on, we're going after him. And nobody walk fast.

lines.text: This is Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine, and it hasn't changed.
lines.script: [quiet, nostalgic] This is Sundial Hollow. I haven't been back here since I was nine, and it hasn't changed.

lines.text: The sundial still says seven o'clock, no matter what time it is.
lines.script: [wry, tender] The sundial still says seven o'clock, no matter what time it is.

lines.text: It's a gold coin, wedged right under the pointer. That's what was holding the shadow at seven. Somebody pushed this in on purpose.
lines.script: [dry, curious] It's a gold coin, wedged right under the pointer. [low, suspicious] That's what was holding the shadow at seven. Somebody pushed this in on purpose.

lines.text: Now the water has drained, and the way to the Deep Pool is open. That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.
lines.script: [determined] Now the water has drained, and the way to the Deep Pool is open. [knowing] That's where Iron-Gill goes to sulk.

lines.text: A man in a long coat stopped the sundial for me. He said if the day never ended, you'd never pack up and go home.
lines.script: [sulky, slow] A man in a long coat stopped the sundial for me. [wounded, small] He said if the day never ended, you'd never pack up and go home.

lines.text: It works because I took the coin out. A man in a long coat stops a sundial so a lonely fish can keep his company. That's a strange favor to do for a fish.
lines.script: [calm, wry] It works because I took the coin out. [low, puzzled] A man in a long coat stops a sundial so a lonely fish can keep his company. [dry, flat] That's a strange favor to do for a fish.

lines.text: All three sets are clear, and Stage 7 just unlocked itself. That's where the fog came from, so that's where my rack is.
lines.script: [tense, quiet] All three sets are clear, and Stage 7 just unlocked itself. [grim, steady] That's where the fog came from, so that's where my rack is.

lines.text: I'm Dana Park, the director, and this is my first feature. Without the costumes we can't shoot, and without a shoot there's no movie.
lines.script: [clipped, stressed] I'm Dana Park, the director, and this is my first feature. [grim, flat] Without the costumes we can't shoot, and without a shoot there's no movie.

lines.text: Those sound like Friction Sprites. Grumpy little monsters, loose on a closed set.
lines.script: [flat, dry] Those sound like Friction Sprites. [deadpan, weary] Grumpy little monsters, loose on a closed set.

lines.text: And it smells like grape fog juice. Only Stage 7 has a fog machine, so my rack must be in Stage 7.
lines.script: [thrilled, curious] And it smells like grape fog juice. [sharp, certain] Only Stage 7 has a fog machine, so my rack must be in Stage 7.

lines.text: Then we clear the Sprites off the sets, one at a time: Main Street, the Western street and New York. After that we deal with Stage 7.
lines.script: [calm, decisive] Then we clear the Sprites off the sets, one at a time: Main Street, the Western street and New York. [methodical, steady] After that we deal with Stage 7.

lines.text: I've been on this lot for forty years, and every bad take was yelled through ME. Nobody ever gets it right.
lines.script: [bitter, grandiose] I've been on this lot for forty years, and every bad take was yelled through ME. [wounded, sulky] Nobody ever gets it right.

lines.text: So I took the costumes. With no costumes there's no take, and with no take there's no BAD take. It's perfect. It's my best work.
lines.script: [smug, scheming] So I took the costumes. [gleeful, triumphant] With no costumes there's no take, and with no take there's no BAD take. [dreamy, self-satisfied] It's perfect. It's my best work.

lines.text: A man in a long coat paid me to do it. One gold coin. He said a day with no takes is a day that never has to end.
lines.script: [brash, tired] A man in a long coat paid me to do it. [low, sly] One gold coin. He said a day with no takes is a day that never has to end.

lines.text: Another gold coin, same as the one in the sundial. First he stops a sundial for a fish, and now he pays a megaphone to stop a movie.
lines.script: [musing, dry] Another gold coin, same as the one in the sundial. First he stops a sundial for a fish, and now he pays a megaphone to stop a movie.

lines.text: Somebody in a long coat really wants things to stand still.
lines.script: [suspicious, thoughtful] Somebody in a long coat really wants things to stand still.

lines.text: The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system, and the bells run on the hallway clocks.
lines.script: [urgent, precise] The Cafetorium doors run on the bell system, and the bells run on the hallway clocks.

lines.text: Until the clocks are right, those doors won't open, and thirty parents are on their way.
lines.script: [anxious, tight] Until the clocks are right, those doors won't open, and thirty parents are on their way.

lines.text: So please set every clock in the hall to exactly seven o'clock. Not seven-thirty, and not six-fifty-nine. Seven.
lines.script: [precise, firm] So please set every clock in the hall to exactly seven o'clock. [insistent, clipped] Not seven-thirty, and not six-fifty-nine. [deadpan, final] Seven.

lines.text: The footprints go into all three rooms and out again, and then east to the Cafetorium. The sign-up sheet went that way.
lines.script: [serious, crisp] The footprints go into all three rooms and out again, and then east to the Cafetorium. [dramatic, low] The sign-up sheet went that way.

lines.text: Then we clear the monsters out of Art, Music and the Gym. After each room, we set its hallway clock to seven o'clock.
lines.script: [calm, even] Then we clear the monsters out of Art, Music and the Gym. After each room, we set its hallway clock to seven o'clock.

lines.text: When all three are right, the Cafetorium opens.
lines.script: [practical, steady] When all three are right, the Cafetorium opens.

lines.text: I have marked a hundred thousand wrong answers in this school. Every quiz, every spelling test and every crooked line.
lines.script: [weary, aggrieved] I have marked a hundred thousand wrong answers in this school. [seething, clipped] Every quiz, every spelling test and every crooked line.

lines.text: But nobody ever grades ME, and nobody ever writes NEAT next to MY work. So tonight I'm grading the grown-ups.

lines.script: [hushed, awed] He's wearing a long coat, like the man Rose saw at the school. [soft, amazed] He's tipping his hat at you.

lines.text: He's the man who handed out the coins. Eight tries to stop our towns, and none of them held.
lines.script: [calm, certain] He's the man who handed out the coins. Eight tries to stop our towns, and none of them held.

lines.text: I don't know his name, but he knows I always make my connection.
lines.script: [calm, certain] I don't know his name, but he knows I always make my connection.

lines.text: A layover is a stop in the middle of a trip. It means this trip isn't over. And neither is he.
lines.script: [calm, warm] A layover is a stop in the middle of a trip. It means this trip isn't over. And neither is he.

lines.text: A gold card came in the mail, addressed to my recliner. It says Priority Member. It's junk mail. They send junk mail to furniture now.
lines.script: [skeptical] A gold card came in the mail, addressed to my recliner. [dry, flat] It says Priority Member. [grumbling] It's junk mail. They send junk mail to furniture now.

lines.text: Don't throw it out, though. It feels warm. Even my knee can feel it.
lines.script: [wary] Don't throw it out, though. [dry, deadpan] It feels warm. Even my knee can feel it.

lines.text: Dad. That card has a little clock on it.
lines.script: [flat, wary] Dad. That card has a little clock on it.

lines.text: Everything has a clock on it. It's junk mail.
lines.script: [offhand, grumbling] Everything has a clock on it. It's junk mail.

lines.text: ...Don't sign anything.
lines.script: [low, wary] ...Don't sign anything.

lines.text: I never sign anything. I didn't sign the mortgage. Your mother did.
lines.script: [wry, grumbling] I never sign anything. [flat, deadpan] I didn't sign the mortgage. Your mother did.

lines.text: The boarding pass from Gate Zero is buzzing in my pocket. Now it says: YOUR LAYOVER IS NOW BOARDING.
lines.script: [dry, curious] The boarding pass from Gate Zero is buzzing in my pocket. [crisp, clear] Now it says: YOUR LAYOVER IS NOW BOARDING.

lines.text: The man in the long coat said my layover would be announced. I think this is it. I have to go back to Gate Zero.
lines.script: [calm, resolved] The man in the long coat said my layover would be announced. [low, certain] I think this is it. I have to go back to Gate Zero.

lines.text: Flight Zero was waiting at the gate with one seat made up. A real pod seat. Somebody upgraded me, and nobody told me why.
lines.script: [dry, suspicious] Flight Zero was waiting at the gate with one seat made up. [deadpan, wary] A real pod seat. Somebody upgraded me, and nobody told me why.

lines.text: You said everybody comes next time, Tata. This is next time.
lines.script: [bright, earnest] You said everybody comes next time, Tata. This is next time.

lines.text: STOP THE PLANE! I don't have a ticket. I have my running shoes, and I just chased my daughters across a whole airport.
lines.script: [frantic, shouting] STOP THE PLANE! [flustered, breathless] I don't have a ticket. [determined, brisk] I have my running shoes, and I just chased my daughters across a whole airport.

lines.text: They ran out of the house in their socks, Tom. Wherever this plane is going, I'm going too. I'm their ride home. And I'm faster than you.
lines.script: [indignant, intense] They ran out of the house in their socks, Tom. [firm, brisk] Wherever this plane is going, I'm going too. [smug, challenging] I'm their ride home. And I'm faster than you.

lines.text: The plane is flying straight into it. Everybody hold on to something. Preferably each other.
lines.script: [calm, steady] The plane is flying straight into it. [warm, dry] Everybody hold on to something. Preferably each other.

lines.text: DING. Welcome to Terminal Infinity, where it is always dusk and every flight is on time.
lines.script: [serene, airy] DING. [soft, hypnotic] Welcome to Terminal Infinity, where it is always dusk and every flight is on time.

lines.text: We flew through the hole in the sky and landed at an airport that isn't on any map.
lines.script: [quiet, wondering] We flew through the hole in the sky and landed at an airport that isn't on any map.

lines.text: Tata, look out the big window. There are two tiny towns floating out there.
lines.script: [hushed, urgent] Tata, look out the big window. [soft, wondering] There are two tiny towns floating out there.

lines.text: The green one on the left is Long Island, and the orange one on the right is Los Angeles.
lines.script: [quiet, dry] The green one on the left is Long Island, and the orange one on the right is Los Angeles.

lines.text: They're both inside glass, like snow globes.
lines.script: [quiet, thoughtful] They're both inside glass, like snow globes.

lines.text: Then this is the layover on your boarding pass.
lines.script: [slow, thinking] Then this is the layover on your boarding pass.

lines.text: It's a place in between our two homes, where everything is on time and nothing is going anywhere.
lines.script: [dry, uneasy] It's a place in between our two homes, where everything is on time and nothing is going anywhere.

lines.text: We're going to find whoever sent me that boarding pass. The only way on is east, down the Endless Concourse.
lines.script: [steady, resolved] We're going to find whoever sent me that boarding pass. [calm, decisive] The only way on is east, down the Endless Concourse.

lines.text: There are nine gates here: Boston, Denver, Seattle, Chicago, Miami and more. Every one of them says PAUSED.
lines.script: [brisk, clipped] There are nine gates here: Boston, Denver, Seattle, Chicago, Miami and more. [flat, uneasy] Every one of them says PAUSED.

lines.text: Each window is a whole town, stopped in the middle of one day. Look, that seagull still has the same fry.
lines.script: [hushed, amazed] Each window is a whole town, stopped in the middle of one day. [bright, delighted] Look, that seagull still has the same fry.

lines.text: Careful. Those are real towns with real people in them, even if they're paused. Don't lick the glass.
lines.script: [calm, dry] Careful. [deadpan] Those are real towns with real people in them, even if they're paused. Don't lick the glass.

lines.text: Gate Infinity is the big door at the far end. I think the man in the long coat is behind it.
lines.script: [calm, wary] Gate Infinity is the big door at the far end. I think the man in the long coat is behind it.

lines.text: But there's a checkpoint in the middle, and somebody is standing in it.
lines.script: [low, alert] But there's a checkpoint in the middle, and somebody is standing in it.

lines.text: You're not on the list. Nobody is ever on the list. That makes you standby passengers. Congratulations, you're number eighteen.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] You're not on the list. Nobody is ever on the list. That makes you standby passengers. Congratulations, you're number eighteen.

lines.text: Me. I've been number seventeen since 1998, waiting for a seat. Nobody gets through this checkpoint ahead of me.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Me. I've been number seventeen since 1998, waiting for a seat. Nobody gets through this checkpoint ahead of me.

lines.text: Hey, babe. A gold boarding pass turned up on the loft door this morning, with my name and Nara's on it. So we got on the plane.
lines.script: [easy, warm] Hey, babe. A gold boarding pass turned up on the loft door this morning, with my name and Nara's on it. So we got on the plane.

lines.text: The airline lost my bag, found Nara, and upgraded us both.
lines.script: [wry, unbothered] The airline lost my bag, found Nara, and upgraded us both.

lines.text: You flew through the hole in the sky too.
lines.script: [quiet, wondering] You flew through the hole in the sky too.

lines.text: I flew through a pink hole in the sky with a dog on a pillow. It was fine. There was a ceramic pot on the drinks cart that was kind of incredible.
lines.script: [easy, amused] I flew through a pink hole in the sky with a dog on a pillow. [warming, excited] It was fine. There was a ceramic pot on the drinks cart that was kind of incredible.

lines.text: So you're TNB. The boyfriend. We finally meet in person.
lines.script: [brisk, guarded] So you're TNB. The boyfriend. We finally meet in person.

lines.text: Okay, everybody. It's always dusk here and nobody has slept, so I'm calling a sleepover before we go any farther.
lines.script: [warm, rallying] Okay, everybody. It's always dusk here and nobody has slept, so I'm calling a sleepover before we go any farther.

lines.text: We have a blanket, a dog, and nine hours of dusk.
lines.script: [easy, amused] We have a blanket, a dog, and nine hours of dusk.

lines.text: They didn't want the good part to end, so they left a piece of it behind and never came back for it.
lines.script: [quiet, aching] They didn't want the good part to end, so they left a piece of it behind and never came back for it.

lines.text: And somebody collected all of it. Every tag has the same little gold clock that's on my coins.
lines.script: [low, dry] And somebody collected all of it. [quiet, grim] Every tag has the same little gold clock that's on my coins.

lines.text: Tata, the Lost Luggage monsters from the Concourse are all in here. And they're all being very polite.
lines.script: [whispering, urgent] Tata, the Lost Luggage monsters from the Concourse are all in here. [earnest, solemn] And they're all being very polite.

lines.text: ...He's been holding a spot here for me. Not for my bag. For me. He wants me to stay.
lines.script: [stunned, thin] ...He's been holding a spot here for me. Not for my bag. [soft, moved] For me. He wants me to stay.

lines.text: You're the man in the long coat. You were in the school parking lot, and on the jet bridge at Gate Zero. You handed out the coins.
lines.script: [wary, steady] You're the man in the long coat. [low, tightening] You were in the school parking lot, and on the jet bridge at Gate Zero. You handed out the coins.

lines.text: My name is Julian Vance. I'm a gate agent, in a way. I have stood at every gate that ever closed.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] My name is Julian Vance. I'm a gate agent, in a way. I have stood at every gate that ever closed.

lines.text: Eight times I gave something lonely a coin and a promise, and eight times your family talked it out of both. Thank you for flying nowhere, Tom.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Eight times I gave something lonely a coin and a promise, and eight times your family talked it out of both. Thank you for flying nowhere, Tom.

lines.text: You are very hard to stop.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] You are very hard to stop.

lines.text: I stopped every town on Earth at its happiest afternoon. A birthday that never ends, or the last day of summer.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I stopped every town on Earth at its happiest afternoon. A birthday that never ends, or the last day of summer.

lines.text: In those towns nobody is ever sad, and nobody is ever late.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] In those towns nobody is ever sad, and nobody is ever late.

lines.text: It should always be this afternoon. Babe, that's what Mr. Washington kept saying when the purple smog came down.
lines.script: [dry, uneasy] It should always be this afternoon. [low, knowing] Babe, that's what Mr. Washington kept saying when the purple smog came down.

lines.text: That was my first try at your street. It would not hold still.
lines.script: [formal, soft] That was my first try at your street. It would not hold still.

lines.text: Only Long Island and Los Angeles kept moving, because you kept flying between them.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Only Long Island and Los Angeles kept moving, because you kept flying between them.

lines.text: Every flight you took moved them along a little, and I was never quick enough to stop you.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Every flight you took moved them along a little, and I was never quick enough to stop you.

lines.text: That is why I sent for you. If you stay here, your two towns will stop as well, and then everyone, everywhere, is safe.
lines.script: [formal, calm] That is why I sent for you. [soft, persuasive] If you stay here, your two towns will stop as well, and then everyone, everywhere, is safe.

lines.text: You told the Mirrorball it could have one dance forever. You told the Last Call it could have midnight forever. They weren't bad. They were lonely.
lines.script: [gentle, steady] You told the Mirrorball it could have one dance forever. You told the Last Call it could have midnight forever. They weren't bad. They were lonely.

lines.text: I think you are too.
lines.script: [low, sincere] I think you are too.

lines.text: I want everyone safe, in the good part, forever. So come in, all of you, and stay. Nobody here has ever been lost.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I want everyone safe, in the good part, forever. So come in, all of you, and stay. Nobody here has ever been lost.

lines.text: That's the nicest offer anyone has ever made me. And I've had the boarding pass for it in my pocket this whole time.
lines.script: [quiet, touched] That's the nicest offer anyone has ever made me. [light, certain] And I've had the boarding pass for it in my pocket this whole time.

lines.text: ...Then I can't let you leave. I'll have to make the last announcement.
lines.script: [trailing off] ...Then I can't let you leave. I'll have to make the last announcement.

lines.text: He lifts his hat. Behind his head, the big door's gold clock spins, and every flap in the terminal clicks at once.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] He lifts his hat. Behind his head, the big door's gold clock spins, and every flap in the terminal clicks at once.

lines.text: The departures board beside the door unfolds, stands up on two legs, and steps out.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] The departures board beside the door unfolds, stands up on two legs, and steps out.

lines.text: It's warm. This is one of the old gold coins he bought up on Long Island. He was using it to hold that gate shut.
lines.script: [quiet, tender] It's warm. [low, thoughtful] This is one of the old gold coins he bought up on Long Island. He was using it to hold that gate shut.

lines.text: And Vance is gone. He slipped away while we were busy with his board.
lines.script: [flat, tired] And Vance is gone. He slipped away while we were busy with his board.

lines.text: Tata, look at the window. The little green town is changing color. It's turning amber, like a caution light.
lines.script: [hushed, uneasy] Tata, look at the window. [worried, quick] The little green town is changing color. [small, uneasy] It's turning amber, like a caution light.

lines.text: He closed Long Island. He couldn't make us stay, so he stopped our home instead.
lines.script: [grim, quiet] He closed Long Island. He couldn't make us stay, so he stopped our home instead.

lines.text: Los Angeles is the orange one. It's the only gate still open, so that's the way we have to go. We'll find a road back to Long Island from there.
lines.script: [calm, gentle] Los Angeles is the orange one. [quiet, heavy] It's the only gate still open, so that's the way we have to go. We'll find a road back to Long Island from there.

lines.text: That's my house number in Los Angeles. The door is going to open onto my street.
lines.script: [quiet, stunned] That's my house number in Los Angeles. [soft, marveling] The door is going to open onto my street.

lines.text: I'm Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I work for Mr. Vance, and I fix places.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I'm Marlowe. Monochrome Marlowe. I work for Mr. Vance, and I fix places.

lines.text: This place has too much going on: too much color, too many porches, and a dog doing something on a lawn.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] This place has too much going on: too much color, too many porches, and a dog doing something on a lawn.

lines.text: He's draining the color out of the whole block. And he did something worse. Look at Mr. Washington. He's not moving.
lines.script: [grim, controlled] He's draining the color out of the whole block. And he did something worse. [sharper, urgent] Look at Mr. Washington. He's not moving.

lines.text: When that man took the color and the music, the warm part of the day had nowhere to go. So it set hard, right around him. That's what amber is: warmth that got stuck.
lines.script: [calm, gentle] When that man took the color and the music, the warm part of the day had nowhere to go. [steady, practical] So it set hard, right around him. That's what amber is: warmth that got stuck.

lines.text: She's in amber too, frozen right in the middle of a sentence.
lines.script: [quiet, solemn] She's in amber too, frozen right in the middle of a sentence.

lines.text: Okay. The whole family is frozen in amber, same as Doña Carmen. Marlowe's grey got in through the front door.
lines.script: [calm, grim] Okay. [low, tense] The whole family is frozen in amber. Marlowe's grey got in through the front door.

lines.text: You work for Vance, and Vance closed Long Island. My mother isn't answering her phone. Where is she?
lines.script: [low, tight] You work for Vance, and Vance closed Long Island. My mother isn't answering her phone. Where is she?

lines.text: Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It's very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making a crisp.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Long Island is under glass now, you know. Mr. Vance put a dome over it. It's very safe. Your mother is in her kitchen, making a crisp.

lines.text: She's been making the same one for hours.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] She's been making the same one for hours.

lines.text: Tell me how to get in.
lines.script: [cold, quiet] Tell me how to get in.

lines.text: He said Long Island is under glass. So Vance sealed it inside a dome, with your mom and dad in it. We'll have to go under the glass, or around it.
lines.script: [calm, practical] He said Long Island is under glass. [easy, bright] So Vance sealed it inside a dome, with your mom and dad in it. We'll have to go under the glass, or around it.

lines.text: Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. We'll start at Sol's cab stand.
lines.script: [focused, steady] Sal and Sol know every road between here and there. [calm, decisive] We'll start at Sol's cab stand.

lines.text: Sol. Vance put a glass dome over Long Island, and my parents are inside it. Sal always says you two know every road there is.
lines.script: [urgent, direct] Sol. Vance put a glass dome over Long Island, and my parents are inside it. Sal always says you two know every road there is.

lines.text: Is there a way under?
lines.script: [low, pleading] Is there a way under?

lines.text: We carry letters. For eleven years we've run mail between Long Island and Los Angeles in the trunks of our cabs.
lines.script: [proud, hushed] We carry letters. For eleven years we've run mail between Long Island and Los Angeles in the trunks of our cabs.

lines.text: Nobody ever opened a bag, and nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.
lines.script: [offhand, smug] Nobody ever opened a bag, and nobody ever asked why two cab companies need a hundred sacks of stamps.

lines.text: Sol, come in. It's Sal, calling from inside the dome. Cab seven says hi. She's fine. She's the only thing in town that's still moving.
lines.script: [crackly, brisk] Sol, come in. It's Sal, calling from inside the dome. [deadpan, dry] Cab seven says hi. She's fine. She's the only thing in town that's still moving.

lines.text: There's a way in, and it's called the Sub-Rail. Sal and I have been boring a tunnel under the Layover from both coasts, as a hobby.
lines.script: [hushed, proud] There's a way in, and it's called the Sub-Rail. Sal and I have been boring a tunnel under the Layover from both coasts, as a hobby.

lines.text: It was supposed to open in 2031. The two halves meet in the middle, right under the dome.
lines.script: [offhand, flat] It was supposed to open in 2031. The two halves meet in the middle, right under the dome.

lines.text: But our drill stopped answering when the dome came down. Something put a chip in it, and now it's loose in the tunnel. Be careful of the Worm.
lines.script: [low, serious] But our drill stopped answering when the dome came down. [grave, urgent] Something put a chip in it, and now it's loose in the tunnel. Be careful of the Worm.

lines.text: I need two dispatchers to stay here on the radio and read the tunnel map to the team.
lines.script: [brisk, urgent] I need two dispatchers to stay here on the radio and read the tunnel map to the team.

lines.text: For years, a man in a long coat bought gold coins from Penny's shop and from mine. He paid double, and he never took his hat off.
lines.script: [quick, uneasy] For years, a man in a long coat bought gold coins from Penny's shop and from mine. [slower, guilty] He paid double, and he never took his hat off.

lines.text: Julian Vance. Those are the coins he handed to every lonely thing we met.
lines.script: [low, grim] Julian Vance. Those are the coins he handed to every lonely thing we met.

lines.text: There are eleven coins left between us, the last of the old gold. They were supposed to be our retirement.
lines.script: [quiet, heavy] There are eleven coins left between us, the last of the old gold. [flat, wistful] They were supposed to be our retirement.

lines.text: Sal says gold remembers being warm. Amber is warmth that got stuck, so maybe warm gold can melt a door in it. That's what Sal says. I don't know.
lines.script: [earnest, unsure] Sal says gold remembers being warm. Amber is warmth that got stuck, so maybe warm gold can melt a door in it. That's what Sal says. I don't know.

lines.text: He's a cab driver.
lines.script: [quick, sheepish] He's a cab driver.

lines.text: The chip makes the Drill dig toward noise. So we make a lot of noise, all together, and it'll come to us.
lines.script: [dry, plotting] The chip makes the Drill dig toward noise. [warm] So we make a lot of noise, all together, and it'll come to us.

lines.text: This cavern is the middle of the tunnel. That wall of amber is the bottom of the dome over Long Island.
lines.script: [hushed, awed] This cavern is the middle of the tunnel. That wall of amber is the bottom of the dome over Long Island.

lines.text: And there's a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.
lines.script: [dry, wary] And there's a hole in the dirt exactly the width of a drill.

lines.text: Be kind to it first, and only hit it if it hits back. Amy, you heal. TNB, I'll go for the hush chip. Everybody else, make some noise.
lines.script: [calm, commanding] Be kind to it first, and only hit it if it hits back. [brisk, steady] Amy, you heal. [rallying, louder] TNB, I'll go for the hush chip. Everybody else, make some noise.

lines.text: A little grey cube just popped out of its side. That's the chip HUSH-9 put in it. It's very quiet.
lines.script: [quiet, dry] A little grey cube just popped out of its side. [wry] That's the chip HUSH-9 put in it. [deadpan] It's very quiet.

lines.text: Okay. From here the Sub-Rail runs the rest of the way, and it comes up through a breach under Grump Hollow, inside the dome.
lines.script: [brisk, practical] Okay. From here the Sub-Rail runs the rest of the way, and it comes up through a breach under Grump Hollow, inside the dome.

lines.text: Sol's putting the girls on the five fifteen handcar.
lines.script: [quick] Sol's putting the girls on the five fifteen handcar.

lines.text: It's a Warden's plate. It's gold armor, and it hums. I like the hum.
lines.script: [weary, formal] It's a Warden's plate. [dreamy] It's gold armor, and it hums. I like the hum.

lines.text: My back doesn't hurt, Tommy, for the first time in eleven years. I made a deal.
lines.script: [steady, distant] My back doesn't hurt, Tommy, for the first time in eleven years. [guarded] I made a deal.

lines.text: As long as I stand guard here, the glass dome stays up over Long Island. That's the deal.
lines.script: [weary, solemn] As long as I stand guard here, the glass dome stays up over Long Island. [weary, final] That's the deal.

lines.text: Dad, that's the same deal he gave a mirrorball, an oven and a squirrel. It isn't safe. It's a freezer.
lines.script: [urgent, gentle] Dad, that's the same deal he gave a mirrorball, an oven and a squirrel. [pained, deadpan] It isn't safe. It's a freezer.

lines.text: Tom. Behind us, down the stairs, something is coming up the tunnel. A lot of grey men with clipboards. Vance's Auditors. I counted fourteen.
lines.script: [low, alert] Tom. [dry, tense] Behind us, down the stairs, something is coming up the tunnel. A lot of grey men with clipboards. [grim, flat] Vance's Auditors. I counted fourteen.

lines.text: Sol's handcar is coming up the tunnel with the girls, and I'll send them up to you. Nara and I will stay and hold the breach.
lines.script: [calm, decisive] Sol's handcar is coming up the tunnel with the girls, and I'll send them up to you. Nara and I will stay and hold the breach.

lines.text: Somebody has to stand at the bottom of the stairs and tell the Auditors no.
lines.script: [steady, easy] Somebody has to stand at the bottom of the stairs and tell the Auditors no.

lines.text: Okay. First we go around him to the porch and help Deedee. Then we deal with Dad. Nobody touches the armor. Not even a little.
lines.script: [calm, firm] Okay. First we go around him to the porch and help Deedee. Then we deal with Dad. Nobody touches the armor. Not even a little.

lines.text: Rose, that includes you.
lines.script: [flat, stern] Rose, that includes you.

lines.text: Amber is warmth that got stuck. She's been baking for nobody for hours, so all that warmth has nowhere to go.
lines.script: [soft, thoughtful] Amber is warmth that got stuck. [quiet, resolved] She's been baking for nobody for hours, so all that warmth has nowhere to go.

lines.text: Maybe somebody just has to eat it.
lines.script: [small, tentative] Maybe somebody just has to eat it.

lines.text: It was the fella I met at the pond, the one in the long coat. He came to the door, very polite. He never took his hat off.
lines.script: [quiet, haunted] It was the fella I met at the pond, the one in the long coat. He came to the door, very polite. He never took his hat off.

lines.text: He said he could stop the aches, and stop the slowing down.
lines.script: [ashamed] He said he could stop the aches, and stop the slowing down.

lines.text: Vance promised you the girls would be safe in the good part, forever. That means he wants to freeze them too.
lines.script: [serious, dry] Vance promised you the girls would be safe in the good part, forever. That means he wants to freeze them too.

lines.text: We already told him no once, and he won't take a second no well.
lines.script: [grim, wary] We already told him no once, and he won't take a second no well.

lines.text: Take the Warden's key, Tommy. It opens the gate, and it opens our front door too. Either way, nobody gets past us.
lines.script: [solemn] Take the Warden's key, Tommy. [firm, steady] It opens the gate, and it opens our front door too. [proud, steady] Either way, nobody gets past us.

lines.text: That is the problem. You are happiest here, so here is where the noise must stop. Mr. Vance has upgraded me. I am now quiet in all directions.
lines.script: [emphasizing] That is the problem. You are happiest here, so here is where the noise must stop. Mr. Vance has upgraded me. I am now quiet in all directions.

lines.text: FINAL FORM.
lines.script: [emphasizing] FINAL FORM.

lines.text: Mr. Vance keeps happy families. The camera catches a good family at the right moment and holds them there, just so.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Mr. Vance keeps happy families. The camera catches a good family at the right moment and holds them there, just so.

lines.text: Nothing ever changes again, and nobody leaves. It's a gift.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Nothing ever changes again, and nobody leaves. It's a gift.

lines.text: (a voice from inside the camera) Hello, Tom. Thank you for flying nowhere.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] (a voice from inside the camera) Hello, Tom. Thank you for flying nowhere.

lines.text: I have waited a very long time for a picture where nobody leaves.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I have waited a very long time for a picture where nobody leaves.

lines.text: I don't want Tom, and I don't want the grown ones. I want the little ones, who still have all their years in them. Those are the ones I want to keep.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I don't want Tom, and I don't want the grown ones. I want the little ones, who still have all their years in them. Those are the ones I want to keep.

lines.text: Girls, close your eyes. Boppy and I are stepping in front of you. To the moon and back.
lines.script: [soft, steady] Girls, close your eyes. [warm, tearful] Boppy and I are stepping in front of you. To the moon and back.

lines.text: Mom! Dad! Get away from the camera!
lines.script: [stricken, desperate] Mom! Dad! Get away from the camera!

lines.text: Nobody moves. Nobody says anything. Deedee and Boppy stepped in front of the camera, and the flash meant for the girls hit them instead.
lines.script: [hushed, stunned] Nobody moves. Nobody says anything. Deedee and Boppy stepped in front of the camera, and the flash meant for the girls hit them instead.

lines.text: In the middle of the Square two stone figures hold each other up, and a small amber light crawls along their joined hands.
lines.script: [slow, aching] In the middle of the Square two stone figures hold each other up, and a small amber light crawls along their joined hands.

lines.text: Then I shall help with your notes, Marlowe.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Then I shall help with your notes, Marlowe.

lines.text: Amber pours out of the camera and over Marlowe. He rises off the ground as a black disc with a burning amber ring around it, like an eclipse.
lines.script: [flat, hushed] Amber pours out of the camera and over Marlowe. [low, tense] He rises off the ground as a black disc with a burning amber ring around it, like an eclipse.

lines.text: Tom. Whatever Marlowe just turned into, it's standing between the girls and the road.
lines.script: [tight, low] Tom. [flat, resolute] Whatever Marlowe just turned into, it's standing between the girls and the road.

lines.text: TOMMY! He's closing glass over the whole town! I have the girls in the cab! GET IN!
lines.script: [panicked, hollering] TOMMY! He's closing glass over the whole town! [frantic, yelling] I have the girls in the cab! GET IN!

lines.text: Vance sealed Long Island inside a snow globe and reeled it up into the sky, with Mom and Dad still standing in the Square.
lines.script: [quiet, subdued] Vance sealed Long Island inside a snow globe and reeled it up into the sky, with Mom and Dad still standing in the Square.

lines.text: Sal drove us out through the Sub-Rail with the meter off. Nobody has said anything since the tunnel.
lines.script: [heavy, soft] Sal drove us out through the Sub-Rail with the meter off. Nobody has said anything since the tunnel.

lines.text: Vance said we know the building: sixty floors, in downtown Los Angeles. That's where he took them.
lines.script: [calm, drained] Vance said we know the building: sixty floors, in downtown Los Angeles. That's where he took them.

lines.text: We rest tonight, and tomorrow we go up.
lines.script: [steady, firm] We rest tonight, and tomorrow we go up.

lines.text: Girls. It's sixty floors. It's going to be hard and strange and not fair.
lines.script: [gentle, level] Girls. [serious, firm] It's sixty floors. It's going to be hard and strange and not fair.

lines.text: Okay. Here's how we do it. We split into two teams of three. Grace, Rose and I take the stairs.
lines.script: [calm, methodical] Okay. Here's how we do it. We split into two teams of three. Grace, Rose and I take the stairs.

lines.text: Amy, TNB and Nara go in through the service ducts to the Archive on floor thirty.
lines.script: [clear, dry] Amy, TNB and Nara go in through the service ducts to the Archive on floor thirty.

lines.text: Which is why I'm going to win this.
lines.script: [smug, determined] Which is why I'm going to win this.

lines.text: I'm calling it. On my mark. Mark!
lines.script: [officious, thrilled] I'm calling it. [yelling, bright] On my mark. Mark!

lines.text: I'm not running. I'm carrying the thermos. Somebody has to.
lines.script: [easy, dry] I'm not running. [amused, unbothered] I'm carrying the thermos. Somebody has to.

lines.text: That's the single saddest thing I have ever heard a lens say.
lines.script: [dry, aghast] That's the single saddest thing I have ever heard a lens say.

lines.text: Mom. Dad. We're coming. We're coming.
lines.script: [fierce, tearful] Mom. Dad. [steady, vowing] We're coming. We're coming.

lines.text: That's exactly the right amount of both.
lines.script: [quiet, warm] That's exactly the right amount of both.

lines.text: I am the man who gave them out. Gold remembers being warm.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I am the man who gave them out. Gold remembers being warm.

lines.text: A coin can hold one warm moment still, for as long as something lonely is willing to hold the coin.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] A coin can hold one warm moment still, for as long as something lonely is willing to hold the coin.

lines.text: Okay. I fix things for a living. Whatever this is, it's structurally unsound.
lines.script: [wary, dry] Okay. [flat, unimpressed] I fix things for a living. Whatever this is, it's structurally unsound.

lines.text: That's not how cups work.
lines.script: [flat, deadpan] That's not how cups work.

lines.text: Tom steps into the Ray and takes all of it. Where he was standing, there is a small warm light, hanging in the air at about the height of his glasses.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Tom steps into the Ray and takes all of it. Where he was standing, there is a small warm light, hanging in the air at about the height of his glasses.

lines.text: Then there is not.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Then there is not.

lines.text: Tom. Tom, answer me. I'm not doing this. I'm not doing this.
lines.script: [pleading, unraveling] Tom. Tom, answer me. [shaking, refusing] I'm not doing this. I'm not doing this.

lines.text: That wave will carry you home. It goes to the place he is from. Hold on to something.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] That wave will carry you home. It goes to the place he is from. Hold on to something.

lines.text: We're not leaving without him!
lines.script: [shouting, desperate] We're not leaving without him!

lines.text: Okay. The wave put us down on Second Avenue, in front of Tom's house. And it's somehow morning.
lines.script: [dazed, shaky] Okay. [quiet, disoriented] The wave put us down on Second Avenue, in front of Tom's house. And it's somehow morning.

lines.text: I know my brother. He's going to turn up late, a little annoyed, with a full explanation, and ask if anybody ate.
lines.script: [tearful, sure] I know my brother. [cracking, tender] He's going to turn up late, a little annoyed, with a full explanation, and ask if anybody ate.

lines.text: The cat is fine. The cat is always fine. The cat isn't even his.
lines.script: [gentle, fond] The cat is fine. [dry, tender] The cat is always fine. The cat isn't even his.

lines.text: Okay. Okay. Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom couldn't put him.
lines.script: [shaky, rallying] Okay. Okay. Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom couldn't put him.

lines.text: And there's exactly one thing in this city that never forgets where things go.
lines.script: [flat, brisk] And there's exactly one thing in this city that never forgets where things go.

lines.text: It's been eleven hours. I've made coffee four times. I haven't drunk any of it. That's not like me.
lines.script: [hollow, exhausted] It's been eleven hours. [quiet, numb] I've made coffee four times. [small, rueful] I haven't drunk any of it. That's not like me.

lines.text: Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom doesn't have a place for.
lines.script: [tired, sharp] Plan. Mom and Dad are stone. Tom is somewhere the Loom doesn't have a place for.

lines.text: And there's one place in this city that keeps everything nobody could put anywhere.
lines.script: [steady, determined] And there's one place in this city that keeps everything nobody could put anywhere.

lines.text: That's not a regular mailbox. That's a mailbox that's thinking about something.
lines.script: [wary, dry] That's not a regular mailbox. [low, deadpan] That's a mailbox that's thinking about something.

lines.text: Vance said the Loom has no place to put him. So maybe he ended up where undelivered things go. We follow the mailbox down.
lines.script: [brisk, thoughtful] Vance said the Loom has no place to put him. [low, certain] So maybe he ended up where undelivered things go. We follow the mailbox down.

lines.text: There are four doors, one for each of us.
lines.script: [quiet, grim] There are four doors, one for each of us.

lines.text: Four people who would never forget him. Behind each door there must be a memory of Tom that only one of us has.
lines.script: [soft, steady] Four people who would never forget him. Behind each door there must be a memory of Tom that only one of us has.

lines.text: If we bring them back to this desk, maybe his name comes back too.
lines.script: [gentle, certain] If we bring them back to this desk, maybe his name comes back too.

lines.text: That's his. I'd know that thermos in the dark.
lines.script: [soft, warm] That's his. [tender, wry] I'd know that thermos in the dark.

lines.text: I erased him. His name was too loud for its line on the page, so I tidied it away. It is not personal. I tidy everything that does not fit.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] I erased him. His name was too loud for its line on the page, so I tidied it away. It is not personal. I tidy everything that does not fit.

lines.text: He's my brother.
lines.script: [low, fierce] He's my brother.

lines.text: Please step back from the desk. I am going to finish erasing the name.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact] Please step back from the desk. I am going to finish erasing the name.

lines.text: Then here's your first delivery route. Take this one pretzel up fifty-nine floors of one tower, and put it in a grandmother's hands.
lines.script: [gentle, encouraging] Then here's your first delivery route. [warm, wry] Take this one pretzel up fifty-nine floors of one tower, and put it in a grandmother's hands.

lines.text: Talking to the stone does nothing. I've checked. What wakes stone up is being warm for a long time, with people close by.
lines.script: [calm, dry] Talking to the stone does nothing. [deadpan, mild] I've checked. [quiet, hopeful] What wakes stone up is being warm for a long time, with people close by.

lines.text: I brought a rock. Lachlan picked it out. Isla ate a different rock. We're keeping a close eye on it.
lines.script: [calm, deadpan] I brought a rock. [flat, dry] Lachlan picked it out. [tired, wry] Isla ate a different rock. We're keeping a close eye on it.

lines.text: Thank you. All of you. I'll put the rock on the mantel.
lines.script: [warm, touched] Thank you. [deadpan, sincere] All of you. I'll put the rock on the mantel.

lines.text: I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. And peppers. My nephew grows them. They're very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.
lines.script: [warm, bustling] I heard there was a situation. I brought lemon bars. [proud, deadpan] And peppers. My nephew grows them. [knowing, matter-of-fact] They're very hot. A man called Boppy would know what to do.

lines.text: I'm the taster. I've tasted nine times. It's for quality.
lines.script: [solemn, earnest] I'm the taster. [dignified, prim] I've tasted nine times. It's for quality.

lines.text: Pack it all up. Sal is outside with cab seven. Mom and Dad are still stone in that snow globe on floor fifty-nine, so we're bringing dinner to them.
lines.script: [warm, resolute] Pack it all up. [firm, dry] Sal is outside with cab seven. [quiet, determined] Mom and Dad are still stone in that snow globe on floor fifty-nine, so we're bringing dinner to them.

lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I'm not even charging.
lines.script: [booming, warm] Cab seven! Everybody in. Bring the lasagna on your lap, it holds the heat. Fifty-nine floors, no stops, I'm not even charging.

lines.text: I'm scared of that tower and I'm going anyway.
lines.script: [proud, generous] I'm scared of that tower and I'm going anyway.

lines.text: Is that lasagna? Who made lasagna? Who's been in my kitchen?
lines.script: [groggy, bewildered] Is that lasagna? [indignant, fussing] Who made lasagna? Who's been in my kitchen?

lines.text: Vance. He's still up there, at the top. He's going to want more than a shelf.
lines.script: [quiet, grim] Vance. [low, level] He's still up there, at the top. He's going to want more than a shelf.

lines.text: That's the Extra Place. Mom has set a place for everybody at every dinner for fifty years, plus one more.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, crisp] That's the Extra Place. Mom has set a place for everybody at every dinner for fifty years, plus one more.

lines.text: A lock that only opens when the whole family shows up? She could have told him how that works.
lines.script: [warm, certain] A lock that only opens when the whole family shows up? [dry, smug] She could have told him how that works.

lines.text: That's the biggest clock I've ever seen. And I have a lot of clocks. They all run fast, for my stomach.
lines.script: [impressed] That's the biggest clock I've ever seen. [dry, grumbling] And I have a lot of clocks. [deadpan] They all run fast, for my stomach.

lines.text: Nara goes first. She's the best at doors.
lines.script: [serious, proud] Nara goes first. [earnest, plain] She's the best at doors.

lines.text: Eight of us, a dog and a thermos. Seconds first, then the sky. Let's go.
lines.script: [calm, dry] Eight of us, a dog and a thermos. [steady, resolved] Seconds first, then the sky. Let's go.

lines.text: It's a very good lock. Whoever made it really cared about the mechanism.
lines.script: [easy, admiring] It's a very good lock. [amused, appreciative] Whoever made it really cared about the mechanism.

lines.text: Each door opens for one person's best skill. Find the door shaped like you, and do the thing you're best at.
lines.script: [calm, thoughtful] Each door opens for one person's best skill. [warm, encouraging] Find the door shaped like you, and do the thing you're best at.

lines.text: I was written out of the schedule. I'm a very stubborn calendar entry.
lines.script: [dry, unbowed] I was written out of the schedule. [deadpan] I'm a very stubborn calendar entry.

lines.text: I was a statue for a week and my back didn't get a single day off. I'd like to file a complaint.
lines.script: [aggrieved] I was a statue for a week and my back didn't get a single day off. [dry, formal] I'd like to file a complaint.

lines.text: Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. That's just a regular Tuesday.
lines.script: [wry, unimpressed] Distance, age, exhaustion, fear. [dry, brisk] That's just a regular Tuesday.

lines.text: It's going to be very, very tired. Be kind about it, and be fast.
lines.script: [gentle, quiet] It's going to be very, very tired. [firm, calm] Be kind about it, and be fast.

lines.text: Up. Everybody up. Breathe. It's a long fight, and we're a long family. We can do this again.
lines.script: [winded, steadying] Up. [warm, resolved] Everybody up. Breathe. [dry, determined] It's a long fight, and we're a long family. We can do this again.

lines.text: He's not attacking us. Look at his hands.
lines.script: [low, alert] He's not attacking us. [quiet, urgent] Look at his hands.

lines.text: They're shaking.
lines.script: [hushed, softening] They're shaking.

lines.text: No hitting. He has done enough to everybody else. Do the thing you're each best at, for him. Everybody. In turn. I'll be last.
lines.script: [quiet, firm] No hitting. He has done enough to everybody else. [gentle, directing] Do the thing you're each best at, for him. Everybody. [dry, steady] In turn. I'll be last.

lines.text: The last one is always the hardest. That's why I put the pepper first.
lines.script: [weary] The last one is always the hardest. [deadpan, wry] That's why I put the pepper first.

lines.text: Everybody up. He's not going anywhere. That's rather the point of him.
lines.script: [tired, warm] Everybody up. [quiet, dry] He's not going anywhere. That's rather the point of him.

lines.text: Honey. That's all of it. That's what living is. It hurts a little, every time, and you do it anyway.
lines.script: [tender, calm] Honey. [soft, loving] That's all of it. [gentle, certain] That's what living is. It hurts a little, every time, and you do it anyway.

lines.text: You don't start them. You stop holding them.
lines.script: [gentle, sure] You don't start them. [soft, kind] You stop holding them.

lines.text: It's five o'clock. It's just five o'clock. It's the best five o'clock I have ever seen.
lines.script: [breathless, awed] It's five o'clock. [soft, marveling] It's just five o'clock. [glowing, heartfelt] It's the best five o'clock I have ever seen.

lines.text: You're doing it right now. Come to dinner.
lines.script: [warm, forgiving] You're doing it right now. [simple, inviting] Come to dinner.

lines.text: And bring a chair. We're short a chair.
lines.script: [kind] And bring a chair. [dry, grumbling] We're short a chair.

lines.text: Mom already set the place. She set it at every dinner for fifty years. There's always one more seat.
lines.script: [tender, proud] Mom already set the place. [softly firm] She set it at every dinner for fifty years. [warm, certain] There's always one more seat.

lines.text: Long Island is a town again. The fountain is running. The library door is open. Someone has already started a pie, which is how you know it's real.
lines.script: [quiet, relieved] Long Island is a town again. The fountain is running. [dry, fond] The library door is open. Someone has already started a pie, which is how you know it's real.

lines.text: Look! Look who's delivering!
lines.script: [excited, bright] Look! Look who's delivering!

lines.text: My pink ribbon! It's still tied in a bow!
lines.script: [thrilled, tender] My pink ribbon! [hushed, amazed] It's still tied in a bow!

lines.text: My stopwatch. It's still running. It's at nine hundred and eleven hours, and some seconds.
lines.script: [stunned, quiet] My stopwatch. [proud, amused] It's still running. It's at nine hundred and eleven hours, and some seconds.

lines.text: My first cup. It's full. It's still warm. I don't know how that's possible and I'm not going to ask.
lines.script: [soft, marveling] My first cup. It's full. [easy, amused] It's still warm. I don't know how that's possible and I'm not going to ask.

lines.text: Cab seven! Everybody in! I'm not charging. I'm not even driving. Look UP.
lines.script: [booming, joyful] Cab seven! Everybody in! [amazed, hushed] I'm not charging. I'm not even driving. Look UP.

lines.text: A SKYWAY TRAIN?! I don't know what to do with my hands! I'm a cab driver!
lines.script: [flabbergasted, overjoyed] A SKYWAY TRAIN?! [panicked, delighted] I don't know what to do with my hands! [flat, bewildered] I'm a cab driver!

lines.text: You're the first passenger. Get in the train.
lines.script: [warm, honored] You're the first passenger. [bright, insistent] Get in the train.

lines.text: I've changed my mind about the man.
lines.script: [grudging, warm] I've changed my mind about the man.

lines.text: That's a good seat to start in.
lines.script: [warm, quiet] That's a good seat to start in.

lines.text: Boppy fell asleep in the recliner somewhere over Nebraska. He says it's the best nap of his life. He says his back has never felt worse.
lines.script: [amused, chatty] Boppy fell asleep in the recliner somewhere over Nebraska. [wry, fond] He says it's the best nap of his life. [dry, giggly] He says his back has never felt worse.

lines.text: Justin is coming out on the next one. He booked his own ticket. He says he cleared the whole weekend.
lines.script: [giddy, disbelieving] Justin is coming out on the next one. He booked his own ticket. He says he cleared the whole weekend.

lines.text: I've been looking at the calendar for an hour to make sure it's real.
lines.script: [stunned, soft] I've been looking at the calendar for an hour to make sure it's real.

lines.text: I made a mug. It has the same handle as the first one. It's exactly too big.
lines.script: [easy, fond] I made a mug. [dry, deadpan] It has the same handle as the first one. It's exactly too big.
